title: Blink an LED
summary: Build your first Arduino circuit and make an LED blink once per second.
wiring: Disconnect USB power before wiring.
Connect digital pin 13 to a 220 Ω resistor.
Connect the resistor to the LED’s long leg (anode).
Connect the LED’s short leg (cathode) to GND.
result: The LED turns on for one second and off for one second repeatedly.
challenge: Change both delay values to create a faster or uneven rhythm.

title: Traffic Light
summary: Control three LEDs in a timed red, yellow and green traffic-light sequence.
wiring: Connect pins 10, 11 and 12 through separate 220 Ω resistors to the red, yellow and green LED anodes.
Connect all three LED cathodes to GND.
result: Only one LED is on at a time, following a repeating traffic-light sequence.
challenge: Add a short red-and-yellow phase before green.

title: Button-Controlled LED
summary: Read a push button and use it to control an LED.
wiring: Connect one side of the button to 5V and the other to pin 2.
Connect a 10 kΩ pull-down resistor between pin 2 and GND.
Connect pin 13 through 220 Ω to the LED anode; connect the cathode to GND.
result: The LED lights while the button is pressed.
challenge: Change the circuit and code to use INPUT_PULLUP.

title: LDR Light Sensor
summary: Measure light with a photoresistor and switch on an LED when the room gets dark.
wiring: Make a voltage divider: 5V → LDR → A0 → 10 kΩ → GND.
Connect pin 13 through 220 Ω to the LED anode and its cathode to GND.
result: The Serial Monitor shows light readings and the LED switches on below the threshold.
challenge: Observe your room’s values and calibrate the threshold.

title: Sound-Activated LED
summary: Use a digital sound sensor module to flash an LED when it detects a loud sound.
wiring: Connect sensor VCC to 5V, GND to GND and digital OUT to pin 2.
Connect pin 13 through 220 Ω to the LED anode; connect the cathode to GND.
result: A loud sound triggers a short LED flash.
challenge: Adjust the module potentiometer and compare sensitivity.

title: Mix Colours with an RGB LED
summary: Control the red, green and blue channels of a common-cathode RGB LED.
wiring: Connect the RGB LED common cathode to GND.
Connect red, green and blue anodes through separate 220 Ω resistors to PWM pins 9, 10 and 11.
result: The LED cycles through three primary colours and purple.
challenge: Create orange, cyan and a smooth colour fade.

title: Moving Flag with a Servo
summary: Move a lightweight paper flag between three angles with an SG90 servo.
wiring: Connect servo signal to pin 9.
Connect servo power to regulated 5V and ground to GND.
If using an external supply, connect its GND to Arduino GND.
result: The servo moves the flag between 0°, 90° and 180°.
challenge: Use a for loop to make the motion smooth.
safety: Do not attach a heavy object to a micro servo. Use a separate regulated supply if the servo causes the Arduino to reset.

title: Mini Emergency Light
summary: Alternate two coloured LEDs to create a compact warning-light pattern.
wiring: Connect pins 8 and 9 through separate 220 Ω resistors to the LED anodes.
Connect both cathodes to GND.
challenge: Design a double-flash pattern using a helper function.

title: Clap-Triggered Light
summary: Detect a clap or other sharp sound and light an LED briefly.
wiring: Connect module VCC to 5V, GND to GND and OUT to pin 2.
Connect pin 13 through 220 Ω to the LED anode and its cathode to GND.
result: A sharp sound produces one controlled flash instead of repeated triggers.
challenge: Count claps and switch the LED state after two detections.

title: Ultrasonic Distance Meter
summary: Measure distance with an HC-SR04 and alert when an object comes close.
wiring: Connect HC-SR04 VCC to 5V, GND to GND, Trig to pin 7 and Echo to pin 6.
Connect pin 13 through 220 Ω to the LED anode and its cathode to GND.
result: Distance appears in centimetres and the LED turns on below 20 cm.
challenge: Make the LED blink faster as an object gets closer.

title: Temperature and Humidity
summary: Read temperature and relative humidity from a DHT11 sensor.
wiring: Connect module VCC to 5V, GND to GND and DATA to pin 4.
For a bare DHT11, add a 10 kΩ pull-up resistor between DATA and 5V.
result: The Serial Monitor updates temperature and humidity about every two seconds.
challenge: Add an LED warning when temperature exceeds a chosen value.

title: Obstacle-Avoiding Robot
summary: Combine a distance sensor and motor driver to make a simple robot avoid obstacles.
wiring: Connect Trig to pin 7 and Echo to pin 6.
Connect L298N IN1–IN4 to pins 4, 5, 8 and 9; keep ENA/ENB jumpers installed.
Power motors from the battery through the driver. Join driver and Arduino grounds.
result: The robot reverses and turns when it detects an object closer than 20 cm.
challenge: Test three thresholds and record which produces the most reliable movement.
safety: Never power DC motors from Arduino pins or the board’s 5V regulator. Check polarity and keep moving parts clear of hair and fingers.

title: Potentiometer LED Dimmer
summary: Turn a potentiometer to control LED brightness.
wiring: Connect the potentiometer outer pins to 5V and GND; connect its centre pin to A0.
Connect PWM pin 9 through 220 Ω to the LED anode and the cathode to GND.
result: LED brightness changes smoothly as the knob turns.
challenge: Reverse the response so clockwise movement makes the LED dimmer.

title: Single-Digit 7-Segment Display
summary: Display the digits 0–9 on a common-cathode 7-segment display.
wiring: Use the display datasheet to identify segments a–g and the common cathodes.
Connect segments a–g through individual 220 Ω resistors to pins 2–8.
Connect both common cathode pins to GND.
result: The display counts from 0 to 9 and repeats.
challenge: Add two buttons to move the number up and down.

title: Joystick Servo Control
summary: Use a joystick’s horizontal axis to position a servo from 0° to 180°.
wiring: Connect joystick VCC to 5V, GND to GND and VRx to A0.
Connect servo signal to pin 9 and its power to regulated 5V.
Join external supply GND to Arduino GND.
result: The servo follows horizontal joystick movement.
challenge: Add a small dead zone around the joystick centre to reduce jitter.
safety: Do not force the servo horn by hand. Use a separate regulated supply if movement resets the board.

title: Automatic Fan Controller
summary: Switch a small DC fan on automatically when a DHT11 reports high temperature.
wiring: Connect DHT11 DATA to pin 4.
Drive the MOSFET gate from pin 6; add 10 kΩ from gate to GND.
Connect fan through the MOSFET and external supply; place the diode reverse-biased across the fan.
Join external supply and Arduino grounds.
result: The fan starts at or above 28 °C and stops below it.
challenge: Add a second, lower off-threshold to prevent rapid switching.
safety: Do not connect the fan directly to an Arduino output. Confirm fan voltage, diode orientation and supply polarity before powering the circuit.

title: PIR Motion Alarm
summary: Detect movement with a PIR sensor and trigger a small buzzer or LED.
materials: Active 5V buzzer or LED with 220 Ω resistor
wiring: Connect PIR VCC to 5V, GND to GND and OUT to pin 2.
Connect a low-current active buzzer to pin 8 and GND, or use an LED with a resistor.
result: After its warm-up period, the PIR activates the output when movement is detected.
challenge: Keep the alarm active for five seconds after the last movement.

title: Light-Following Robot
summary: Compare two light sensors and steer a two-motor robot toward the brighter side.
wiring: Build two 5V LDR voltage dividers and connect their centres to A0 and A1.
Connect L298N IN1–IN4 to pins 4–7; keep ENA/ENB jumpers installed.
Power motors externally and join driver and Arduino grounds.
result: The robot moves forward under balanced light and turns toward the brighter sensor.
challenge: Calibrate the dead-band and shield the two LDRs from each other.
safety: Power motors through the driver and a suitable battery only. Keep the robot on a clear floor and restrain it during the first powered test.

title: Mini Digital Clock
summary: Read time from a DS3231 real-time clock and show it on an I²C LCD.
wiring: Connect both modules to 5V and GND.
Connect both SDA pins to A4 and both SCL pins to A5 on the Uno.
Check the LCD address with an I²C scanner; 0x27 is common.
result: The LCD displays the current time and date while the RTC keeps time when unplugged.
challenge: Add two buttons to choose between clock and temperature views.
